paper.title: SmartWay: Enhanced Waypoint Prediction and Backtracking for Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation
paper.central_claim: SmartWay combines an enhanced trained waypoint predictor (DINOv2 encoder, masked cross-attention RGB-D fusion, occupancy-aware loss) with a zero-shot GPT-4o navigator using history-aware single-expert prompting, adaptive multi-step planning and a one-step backtrack action; it claims zero-shot SOTA on R2R-CE (SR 29, SPL 22.46 on 100 episodes), better waypoint quality on MP3D, and real-world validation on a Turtlebot 4.
paper.claim_scope_note: R2R-CE results are the Open-Nav 100-episode subset; real world is 25 author-defined instructions in one indoor environment; 'first exploration of MLLMs for zero-shot VLN-CE' sits beside a MapGPT-CE-GPT4o row in the paper's own Table I.

preliminary_judgment: Written before opening seat totals. Operation: a supervised waypoint predictor (trained 300 epochs on MP3D, occupancy BCE against a depth-derived navigability mask) proposes up to 5 candidates; GPT-4o chooses among image-backed action options with multi-scale turns, RAM object tags, a running plan and history, and may pick 'move back to last position'. Evidence: R2R-CE 100 episodes, single run, 3 m criterion: SR 29 vs Open-Nav-GPT4 19 (different backbone) and MapGPT-CE-GPT4o 7; Table V 2x2 (predictor x backtrack) with GPT-4o fixed: 24/28/26/29 SR, i.e. a few episodes each; the history/RAM/turn-scale/plan components are never ablated while row #1 (original predictor, no backtrack) already reaches 24. Table V's check-mark columns are lost in the material and the prose's 'NE is decreased to 7.11' for #3 conflicts with the table (row #3 NE 6.73; 7.11 is row #2), though the prose's SR 26 (#3) and collision 0.067 -> 0.044 (#1 -> #2) fix the row mapping. Waypoint ablation is cumulative; occupancy loss lifts %Open 82.15 -> 87.26 (a metric close to what the loss optimizes). Real world: 25 instructions once each, 2 m criterion, RecBERT 5/25, no-backtrack 6/25, full 9/25. No latency/API cost. Initial view: modest, directionally consistent gains with weak statistics; sim-to-real counted with a real baseline.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Both seats agree; confirmed: the sim-trained predictor and zero-shot navigator run on a Turtlebot 4 in an unseen indoor environment with 25 counted instructions, an explicit 2 m criterion and same-robot baselines (EVIDENCE.md sim-to-real with trial counts). Lower bound: one trial per instruction, one environment.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On the Open-Nav 100-episode R2R-CE subset, the GPT-4o navigator with the enhanced predictor and backtrack reaches SR 29 / SPL 22.46 (single run), above the listed zero-shot rows (Open-Nav with a different backbone); the 2x2 shows predictor and backtrack each adding 2-4 episodes; occupancy loss raises the MP3D %Open to 87.26; on 25 real instructions SR is 9/25 vs 6/25 without backtrack and 5/25 for RecBERT.
not_supported_as_stated: state of the art attributable to the harness (backbones differ; navigator prompt components un-ablated)
first MLLM exploration of zero-shot VLN-CE
assessment.not_claimed: No reproduction; all results are author reports.

G.reason: Concrete deficits (obstacle-blind waypoint prediction, text-only perception and missing recovery in zero-shot VLN-CE navigators) with named lineage (Hong et al., ETPNav, MapGPT, Open-Nav) and numbers; the 'first exploration' priority claim conflicts with the paper's own MapGPT-CE-GPT4o row (agg:E002). Both seats agree at 3.

M.reason: Occupancy loss targets obstacle-placed waypoints and backtrack targets irreversible errors, each with testable predictions (%Open, collisions, OSR/SR); the mechanism of history/RAM prompting is thin. Both seats agree.

X.reason: Predictor side fully reconstructible (loss, mask, hyperparameters), but the navigator's operative interface - prompt text (only in a figure absent from the material), history format, plan format, stop rule and real-world motion execution - is underspecified, and the backtrack is a one-step opposite move. Anchor 2: main steps described, key interface conditions unclear.

measurement.reason: Anchors v2 'all results single trials without repeats -> <=2': every simulated episode and real instruction is run once. Success criteria (3 m sim, 2 m real) and denominators (100, 25) are explicit; Table V's lost check marks and the prose/table NE conflict reduce readout reliability.

causality.reason: 2x2 predictor x backtrack with GPT-4o fixed and the real with/without-backtrack comparison give directionally consistent evidence; but the main gap over Open-Nav mixes backbones, row #1 already reaches 24 so un-ablated prompt components carry most of it, and effects are a few episodes. Both seats agree.

holdout.reason: Predictor trained on MP3D and evaluated val-unseen; navigator zero-shot; deployed sim-to-real on a new embodiment in an unseen environment with a same-protocol baseline, where the ordering is retained (9 vs 6 vs 5 of 25). Deducted from 4 for undisclosed prompt/hyperparameter development episodes, author-defined instructions and a single environment.

statistics.reason: Anchors v2: single run per configuration, no CI, differences of 2-5 episodes (3 of 25 real), and the OSR-SR stop gap is reported but not decomposed -> <=1.

cost.reason: Not entirely unreported: hardware, trajectory length per configuration and an encoder-size parity statement are given (agg:E003); but no latency, GPT-4o call count, tokens, USD or matched budget. Between anchor 0 and 2.

son55_value.reason: 完整 HTML 全文含全部方法与实验；无独立附录；Fig 3 提示文本仅图中。

resolutions.reason: Primary sub: plan revision from fresh observations plus an explicit backtrack action is the model's own revise loop during construction -> C25 (son55; same rule as 2609.39915/2609.26360). Supporting: the occupancy loss is a soft auxiliary loss relearned from data, which structural_prior_encoding explicitly contrasts with ('satisfied by construction rather than relearned'); C17 also does not fit (pairing geometry). So no supporting card (sol).

The navigator interface that carries the zero-shot claim (prompt text, history/plan format, stop rule, real motion execution) is not reconstructible from the text; son55 itself notes the prompt is only in a figure.
Anchors v2 binding clause 'all results single trials without repeats -> <=2' applies; the Table V readout problem is an additional deduction son55 listed but did not apply.

Unlike a pure dev-overlap case, the paper has a counted sim-to-real deployment on a new embodiment with a same-protocol baseline and retained ordering; the undisclosed prompt development keeps it below 4. Distinguishes from 2609.39915 (real baselines were supplied aggregates, no criterion) where holdout is 2.
Single runs with 2-5 episode differences and no decomposition of the OSR-SR gap fall under the v2 '<=1' clause; reporting OSR and collisions as metrics is not a failure analysis.

not_reported requires that nothing applicable is reported; the paper gives hardware, trajectory length per configuration and an encoder-size compute-parity statement (agg:E003). Too thin for 2 (no budget or latency).
